title: Portable calibration: keep the ordinary winner
objective: Make readings from the supplied sensor comparable with a shared reference. Keep the measurement and provenance inspectable. Reject a consequential arithmetic defect. Investigate a voluntary arrangement that small participants can afford, and retain an ordinary solution whenever it achieves the same outcome at lower complete cost.

sources.title: Authored teaching calibration points
sources.content: Raw 100 maps to reference 0; raw 500 maps to reference 10000. Reference units are integer milli-units. Affinity on [100,500] is an assumption, not an observed physical fact.

opportunities.title: Portable reference passport with independently replayable arithmetic
opportunities.hypothesis: An inspectable conversion and source record could make shared reference access usable across laboratories without requiring each to own an instrument. Actual measurement quality and participant willingness remain untested.
assumptions: All sensor values, costs, benefits and outside options are synthetic teaching inputs.
The raw/reference relationship is assumed affine on [100,500]; two endpoints do not establish physical linearity, stability or uncertainty.
No actual customer, supplier quote, willingness to pay, funding receipt, contract or physical measurement is represented.
The proposal was authored by an included assistant from this objective during product development; it is not autonomous discovery by the application or evidence of scientific novelty.

experiment.procedure: Construct (reading - 100) × 25, retain a calibrated-range flag, compare frozen numerical cases against direct algebra, reject an omitted offset, and recompute every participant payoff.
experiment.acceptance: Exact agreement on declared numerical cases; protected independently prepared cases are evaluated separately. No participant falls below its declared outside option.
experiment.failure: Incorrect conversion, unrecognized range violation, unfavorable participant payoff or conventional complete route advantage prevents an invention-superiority claim.
